title: Core: Zoom tool reimplementation
body:
Contributes to https://github.com/storybookjs/storybook/issues/33245
Telescopes on https://github.com/storybookjs/storybook/pull/33290

## What I did

This is an almost complete rewrite of the Zoom tool. Notable changes:
- Tool is moved from the left-hand side of the toolbar to the right-hand side.
- The three toolbar items have been replaced with a single button, showing the current zoom percentage.
- Zooming now uses a set of predefined levels rather than a zoom factor (multiplier), for more predictability and consistency with other software (e.g. DevTools).
- Keyboard shortcuts `⌥+`, `⌥-` and `⌥0` have been added for quick access.
- Custom zoom percentages are now supported, even outside of the usual 25-400% range.
- The Viewports feature has been updated to play well with zooming, so that the canvas scales along with the zoom level.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8b7fea7f-72a7-4704-aabd-b0d217e5c449


## Checklist for Contributors

### Testing

<!-- Please check (put an "x" inside the "[ ]") the applicable items below to communicate how to test your changes -->

#### The changes in this PR are covered in the following automated tests:

- [x] stories
- [ ] unit tests
- [ ] integration tests
- [ ] end-to-end tests

#### Manual testing

- Find the zoom button at the right-hand side of the toolbar. Confirm it shows 100% initially.
- Click it to reveal the zoom controls and try each of the options there to see if they behave as you would expect.
- Focus the input field and use the up/down arrow keys to change the zoom level. Enter a manual value as well.
- Find the viewport controls in the toolbar and select one (e.g. Small mobile). Confirm the zoom controls work with the viewports (the whole viewport zooms, not just the iframe contents).
- Try the keyboard shortcuts `⌥+`, `⌥-` and `⌥0`.

  * Shortcut badge for displaying keyboard shortcuts
  * Redesigned Zoom tool with numeric input, presets (50/100/200%) and shortcuts
  * Viewport size controls and improved drag handles

* **Refactor**

  * Shortcut display extracted to a reusable component

* **Tests**

* **Improvements**

**Add scale validation to prevent invalid CSS values from zero or negative zoom.**

The manual zoom input in `zoom.tsx` (lines 93-98) validates only `!Number.isNaN(zoomLevel)`, allowing users to enter 0 or negative values. When scale is 0 or negative, the calculation at lines 347-348 produces `Infinity%` or negative percentages, breaking the layout. While predefined zoom buttons enforce bounds (0.25–4), manual percentage input does not.

Add validation to the zoom input handler:

<details>
<summary>Suggested fix</summary>

```diff
 setValue={(value: string) => {
   const zoomLevel = parseInt(value, 10) / 100;
-  if (!Number.isNaN(zoomLevel)) {
+  if (!Number.isNaN(zoomLevel) && zoomLevel > 0) {
     zoomTo(zoomLevel);
   }
 }}
```

</details>

Alternatively, add a defensive guard in `Viewport.tsx` at the frameStyles useMemo to clamp scale to a safe minimum.

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```
In @code/core/src/manager/components/preview/Viewport.tsx around lines 274 -
286, frameStyles can produce invalid CSS when scale is zero or negative
(resulting in Infinity% or negative sizes); in the frameStyles useMemo clamp the
incoming scale to a safe minimum (e.g., minScale = 0.01 or the same lower bound
used by the zoom controls) before computing width/height so
parseNumber(width/height) times clampedScale is always finite and positive;
reference the parseNumber function and the frameStyles useMemo and apply the
clamp to the local scale variable derived from the scale prop (or also add
equivalent validation in the manual zoom handler in zoom.tsx to reject/normalize
<=0 values).
```

</details>

**Address TypeScript strict mode violations in ZoomIFrame component.**

The zoom calculation using `(1 / scale) * 100%` for dimensions combined with `scale(${scale})` transform is mathematically correct. However, the component has multiple TypeScript strict mode violations that must be resolved per project guidelines:

- Line 12: `@ts-expect-error (non strict)` on `iframe` property assignment
- Line 17: `@ts-expect-error (non strict)` on `iFrameRef.current` assignment  
- Line 40: `@ts-expect-error (non strict)` on `contentDocument.body.style` access

These should use proper TypeScript types (e.g., `HTMLIFrameElement | null` for the property, safe null checks) rather than error suppression.

Additionally, the `ZoomIFrame` component lacks test coverage. Consider adding tests for zoom functionality at various scale levels (e.g., 0.5x, 1x, 2x) to verify no visual regressions occur.

_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟡 Minor_

**Fix cursor positioning logic for edge case.**

Line 94-96: The condition `if (input && index > 0)` will skip setting the cursor when `index === 0`, but 0 is a valid position (at the start of the input). This means if the input value is `"100"` (all digits), the cursor won't be positioned.



<details>
<summary>🔧 Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
       requestAnimationFrame(() => {
         const input = inputRef.current;
         const index = input?.value.search(/[^\d.]/) ?? -1;
-        if (input && index > 0) {
+        if (input && index >= 0) {
           input.setSelectionRange(index, index);
         }
       });
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```
In @code/core/src/manager/components/preview/NumericInput.tsx around lines 91 -
99, The cursor positioning in setInputSelection incorrectly skips when index ===
0; change the condition so it triggers for any non-negative index (e.g., use
index >= 0 or index !== -1) and still guard input exists before calling
input.setSelectionRange(index, index). Update the useCallback block that
references inputRef.current and the computed index (const index =
input?.value.search(/[^\d.]/) ?? -1) to check for index >= 0 (or index !== -1)
instead of index > 0 so the cursor is set at the start of the field as well.
```

</details>

**Use a fallback implementation compatible with ES2020.**

The `findLast` method is an ES2023 feature. Since Storybook targets ES2020, this will fail in browsers without ES2023 support.

<details>
<summary>Suggested fix</summary>

```diff
  const zoomOut = useCallback(() => {
-    const lowerZoomLevel = ZOOM_LEVELS.findLast((level) => level < value);
+    const lowerZoomLevel = [...ZOOM_LEVELS].reverse().find((level) => level < value);
    if (lowerZoomLevel) {
      set(lowerZoomLevel);
    }
  }, [set, value]);
```
</details>

<!-- suggestion_start -->

<details>
<summary>📝 Committable suggestion</summary>

> ‼️ **IMPORTANT**
> Carefully review the code before committing. Ensure that it accurately replaces the highlighted code, contains no missing lines, and has no issues with indentation. Thoroughly test & benchmark the code to ensure it meets the requirements.

```suggestion

    const lowerZoomLevel = [...ZOOM_LEVELS].reverse().find((level) => level < value);
    if (lowerZoomLevel) {
      set(lowerZoomLevel);
    }
  }, [set, value]);
```

</details>

ES2020 targets; replace it with an ES2020-compatible search over ZOOM_LEVELS

function and then call set(lowerZoomLevel) when found; update references to

**Align shortcut display key with registered key and stabilize callback dependencies.**

3. **Note on `Array.at()` and `Array.findLast()`:** The current browserslist (Chrome ≥131, Firefox ≥136, Edge ≥134) supports both methods natively (at() since Chrome 92, findLast() since Chrome 110), so no polyfill is needed.

}>(function ZoomWrapper({ set, value }) {

+  const valueRef = useRef(value);
